sentences.en: My name is Taffy Brodesser-Eckner and I'm a writer for The New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫塔菲·布罗德瑟-埃克纳，我是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: Recently, one of my oldest friends told me that her father was dying.
sentences.zh: 最近，我的一位老朋友告诉我，她的父亲快要去世了。

sentences.en: I've known her father since I was 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 我从15岁起就认识她的父亲了。

sentences.en: And he has been asking me for years to tell his story about how he survived the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直请求我讲述他幸免于大屠杀的故事。

sentences.en: I always said no.
sentences.zh: 我总是拒绝。

sentences.en: I said no because I felt that I had grown up inundated with Holocaust stories.
sentences.zh: 我拒绝是因为我觉得自己从小就被大屠杀的故事淹没了。

sentences.en: I sort of hate telling Holocaust stories.
sentences.zh: 我有点讨厌讲大屠杀的故事。

sentences.en: I hate the Holocaust as a reasonable person should.
sentences.zh: 作为一个正常人，我理所当然地讨厌大屠杀。

sentences.en: And part of my coming of age was to leave the Holocaust behind, was to figure out who I
sentences.zh: 我成长的一部分就是把大屠杀抛在脑后，去弄清楚我作为一个美国人、

sentences.en: was as an American, as a Jew, without this sort of story that tends to follow Jewish Americans around.
sentences.zh: 一个犹太人到底是谁，而不必带着这种往往会纠缠犹太裔美国人的故事。

sentences.en: So I resisted.
sentences.zh: 所以我抗拒。

sentences.en: I would put him off or say no.
sentences.zh: 我总是敷衍他或者拒绝。

sentences.en: So, and then I found out he was dying.
sentences.zh: 然后，我得知他快不行了。

sentences.en: He had cancer.
sentences.zh: 他得了癌症。

sentences.en: And I was so sad about it.
sentences.zh: 我为此感到无比难过。

sentences.en: I felt like, what have I been doing not telling this man's story?
sentences.zh: 我觉得，我怎么能一直不把这个男人的故事写出来呢？

sentences.en: He was seven years old for the duration of the time that the Nazis occupied Budapest, which is where he was from.
sentences.zh: 纳粹占领布达佩斯期间，他一直是个七岁的孩子，那是他的故乡。

sentences.en: And he was 87 when I found out he was sick.
sentences.zh: 当我得知他生病时，他已经87岁了。

sentences.en: It created a sort of panic in me that if the youngest people who survived Nazi persecution were dying, then there would be nobody to tell these stories.
sentences.zh: 这在我心中制造了一种恐慌：如果连经历过纳粹迫害最年轻的人都在离去，那就没人来讲述这些故事了。

sentences.en: And so I decided that I would.
sentences.zh: 于是我决定由我来写。

sentences.en: So I started writing the story and people would ask me, oh, I heard you're writing a Holocaust survivor story.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始写这个故事，人们会问我，哦，我听说你在写一个大屠杀幸存者的故事。

sentences.en: What camp was he in?
sentences.zh: 他待过哪个集中营？

sentences.en: And the man I'm writing about lived in Budapest and was sent into hiding in several different places, but he was not in a concentration camp.
sentences.zh: 而我笔下的这个人住在布达佩斯，曾被送到几个不同的地方隐蔽，但他并没有去过集中营。

sentences.en: And people were strange about that.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到有些异样。

sentences.en: But there's this idea that in order to write about the Holocaust, you have to write its most brutal stories in order to make a point about what the Holocaust was.
sentences.zh: 但有一种观点认为，要想写大屠杀，就必须写它最残酷的故事，以此来证明大屠杀到底是什么。

sentences.en: But actually, the whole problem with the Holocaust, other than the fact that it was the Holocaust, is that it touched every single Jew.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，大屠杀的全部问题——除了它本身就是大屠杀这个事实之外——在于它触及了每一个犹太人。

sentences.en: And at some point in thinking about this and in hearing all of the stories that I heard,
sentences.zh: 在思考这件事、听了所有这些故事的某个时刻，

sentences.en: I came to understand that I, too, was from a family of Holocaust survivors.
sentences.zh: 我开始明白，其实我也来自一个大屠杀幸存者家庭。

sentences.en: In my family, we never spoke about the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 在我的家庭里，我们从不谈论大屠杀。

sentences.en: When I asked my grandmother what it was like for her as a child, well, it was the war.
sentences.zh: 当我问祖母她小时候是什么感觉时，好吧，那就是战争。

sentences.en: There was a vague war.
sentences.zh: 那是一场模糊的战争。

sentences.en: There was a point at which I was nine or ten years old, and I realized that the war they were talking about was the Holocaust I was learning about in school all the time.
sentences.zh: 大约在我九、十岁的时候，我突然意识到他们口中的战争就是我一直在学校里学到的大屠杀。

sentences.en: I went to a Jewish day school, and we didn't talk about it, and we didn't describe ourselves as Holocaust survivors, and we were surrounded by people who did.
sentences.zh: 我上的是一所犹太全日制学校，我们不谈论它，我们不把自己描述为大屠杀幸存者，尽管我们身边都是这样的人。

sentences.en: So over the course of reporting this story, I called my mother, and I asked her, do you think of us as a survivor family?
sentences.zh: 因此，在报道这个故事的过程中，我打电话给母亲，问她，你觉得我们是幸存者家庭吗？

sentences.en: And she said, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 她说，你在说什么？

sentences.en: Of course we are.
sentences.zh: 我们当然是。

sentences.en: Your Hebrew middle name is the name of your grandfather's sister who was killed in the
sentences.zh: 你的希伯来语中间名就是你祖父的妹妹的名字，她在

sentences.en: Lodz ghetto, and my mother was named after her grandmother who suffered the same fate.
sentences.zh: 罗兹隔都遇害了，而我母亲的名字也是为了纪念她遭遇同样命运的祖母而取的。

sentences.en: She said, of course we're a survivor family.
sentences.zh: 她说，我们当然是一个幸存者家庭。

sentences.en: And I got off the phone, and I was very emotional.
sentences.zh: 我挂了电话，内心非常激动。

sentences.en: And I called my kids into the living room, and I said to them, kids, do you realize that we are from a Holocaust survivor family?
sentences.zh: 我把孩子们叫到客厅，对他们说，孩子们，你们意识到我们来自一个大屠杀幸存者家庭吗？

sentences.en: And they said, of course we do.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们当然知道。

sentences.en: I guess part of me not understanding it was part of the same wish I had in running away from it, which was a refusal to define myself in those terMs.
sentences.zh: 我想我之所以无法理解这一点，和我逃避它的愿望如出一辙，那就是拒绝用这些术语来定义自己。

sentences.en: But of course, like anything else you run away from, you arrive at a certain age and realize that the running away from it, that is its own way of engaging in your culture.
sentences.zh: 但当然，就像你逃避的任何其他事情一样，当你到了某个年纪，就会发现逃避本身就是参与你文化的一种方式。

sentences.en: It's not that inherited trauma gets diluted as generations pass, but it's also not as if you can deny your inheritance.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说代际传承的创伤会随着时间的流逝而淡化，但你也不是说否认就能否认得了你的传承。

sentences.en: The trauma just doesn't look the same as it did in the prior generation.
sentences.zh: 这种创伤只是看起来与前一代人不同了。

sentences.en: It morphs, it changes, it becomes its own thing that you might not even recognize as inherited trauma in the first place.
sentences.zh: 它畸变了、改变了，变成了它自己的形态，以至于你一开始甚至可能认不出那是代际创伤。

sentences.en: I came to understand over the course of this story that there are people like me who refused the Holocaust as their burden.
sentences.zh: 通过这个故事，我逐渐明白，有像我这样的人，拒绝把大屠杀当作自己的重担。

sentences.en: But it's all of our burden.
sentences.zh: 但这是我们所有人的重担。

sentences.en: Running away from it is its own burden.
sentences.zh: 逃避它本身就是一种重担。

sentences.en: So I finally wrote it.
sentences.zh: 所以我终于把它写了下来。

sentences.en: I finally wrote the Holocaust story I said I would never write.
sentences.zh: 我终于写下了那个我曾说绝不会写的大屠杀故事。

sentences.zh: 在这个故事里，它们无处不在。

sentences.en: I hung up the phone, and I thought about Mr. Lindenblatt.
sentences.zh: 我挂了电话，想起了林登布拉特先生。

sentences.en: His first name was Yehuda, though it feels seditious to even say the first name of a childhood friend's father.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫耶胡达，不过直呼童年朋友父亲的名字总让人觉得有点大逆不道。

sentences.en: I thought about how he was a runner, back when it was just called jogging.
sentences.zh: 我想起他是个跑步爱好者，那是这还只被称为慢跑的年代。

sentences.en: How he drank rice milk before alternative milks were the style.
sentences.zh: 想起在替代奶流行之前，他就开始喝米奶了。

sentences.en: How he would walk through the house in his running shorts and no shirt, which absolutely none of the other dads did.
sentences.zh: 想起他会穿着跑步短裤、光着膀子在屋里走来走去，其他爸爸绝对没有人会这么做。

sentences.en: How he thanklessly and happily took on the burden of driving Alana and me both ways to our losing basketball games, and our even losing-her-play rehearsals.
sentences.zh: 想起他毫无怨言、高高兴兴地承担起接送我和伊拉娜去参加那些总是输球的篮球赛，以及那些连演出的排练也惨淡收场的戏剧排练的重任。

sentences.en: We were in Brigadoon together, don't ask.
sentences.zh: 我们一起演过《奇幻岛》，别问了。

sentences.en: When my mother was pregnant with my youngest sister.
sentences.zh: 当时我母亲正怀着我的小妹妹。

sentences.en: How he taught me to say, hello, how are you, in his native Hungarian, which has proved useful in my life twice so far.
sentences.zh: 想起他教我说匈牙利语的“你好，你好吗”，这到目前为止在我的生活中已经派上过两次用场。

sentences.en: How he walked around on Shabbat with a walkie-talkie, because in addition to working at his family's
sentences.zh: 想起他在安息日拿着对讲机走来走去，因为除了在他们家中城 Midtown 的家族

sentences.en: camera store in Midtown, he volunteered for the Jewish ambulance service in Manhattan Beach near their home.
sentences.zh: 照相馆工作外，他还志愿加入他们家附近曼哈顿海滩的犹太救护队。

sentences.en: And I thought about the fact that Mr. Lindenblatt survived the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 我还想到了林登布拉特先生在大屠杀中幸存下来的事实。

sentences.en: In my neighborhood in Brooklyn, in the surrounding neighborhoods too, it seemed as if everyone was a survivor.
sentences.zh: 在我布鲁克林的社区里，以及周边的社区里，似乎每个人都是幸存者。

sentences.en: However, we all had the Holocaust in our past to varying degrees.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们过去经历大屠杀的程度各不相同。

sentences.en: We knew whose fathers were Holocaust survivors, and whose grandmothers had numbers on their arms, and whose aunts never made it out of the ghetto.
sentences.zh: 我们知道谁的父亲是大屠杀幸存者，谁的祖母手臂上有数字，谁的阿姨没能活着离开集中营。

sentences.en: All discussed as part of our Holocaust education at the Yeshiva High School that Alana and I attended in Queens.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我和伊拉娜在皇后区就读的叶史瓦高中大屠杀教育的一部分。

sentences.en: And let me tell you, on the matter of the Holocaust, we were educated.
sentences.zh: 说实话，在大屠杀这件事上，我们可是受过教育的。

sentences.en: I need to disclose to you that yes, I am hyperbolic, and that I know that hyperbole combined with
sentences.zh: 我得向你们坦白，是的，我用了夸张的手法，我也知道夸张结合了

sentences.en: the way the brain rounds down when it has been trying to make a point for too many years is deadly, but here it is anyway.
sentences.zh: 大脑在试图多年来证明一个观点时倾向于将数据抹平的心理是致命的，但事实就是如此。

sentences.en: In my most bitter moments, and times when I realize how much of my foundational education
sentences.zh: 在我最痛苦的时刻，当我意识到我大部分的基础教育

sentences.en: was given over to the war, and how little was given over to, say, gym, or art, or the other
sentences.zh: 都贡献给了战争，而留给诸如体育、艺术或其他

sentences.en: humanities that would have helped me in life, or at the very least in work meetings, I say I went to a Holocaust high school, a magnet school for Jewish death studies.

sentences.en: I say my school taught us master's-level World War II history, and also just enough math and science to pass the New York State Regents exaMs.
sentences.zh: 我会说我的学校教给我们的是硕士级别的二战历史，以及刚刚好能通过纽约州立考试的数学和科学。

sentences.en: I'm joking.
sentences.zh: 我在开玩笑。

sentences.en: But am I?
sentences.zh: 但真的是吗？

sentences.en: I left high school having read Macbeth not once, but Elie Wiesel's Night three times over the course of my education.
sentences.zh: 我高中毕业时读《麦克白》读了一遍，而埃利·维瑟尔的《夜》在我的求学过程中却读了三遍。

sentences.en: I can probably auto-complete any sentence from Anne Frank's diary if you start me off with three words.
sentences.zh: 只要你给我开个三个词的头，我大概能自动补全安妮·弗兰克日记里的任何一句话。

sentences.en: I have forgotten more about the Holocaust than I ever knew about the American Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我对大屠杀的了解，远远超过了我对美国独立战争的了解。

sentences.en: Again, I'm mostly hyperbolic here.
sentences.zh: 再次声明，我这里多半是在夸张。

sentences.en: Lots of people hated their high schools, and even more people of my generation have aged up to find that their formal education let them down in some crucial way or another.
sentences.zh: 很多人都讨厌他们的高中，而且我这一代有更多人在长大后发现他们的正规教育在某处关键地方让他们失望了。

sentences.en: There were other yeshivas that were more focused on their students' prospects for success, and a few of my classmates became doctors and lawyers.
sentences.zh: 还有其他更注重学生成功前景的叶史瓦学校，我的几个同班同学后来成了医生和律师。

sentences.en: Hey, maybe it was a fine high school, and I was just a terrible student, which I absolutely was.
sentences.zh: 嘿，也许那是一所不错的高中，而我只是个糟糕的学生，我确实是。

sentences.en: I did fail several classes and had to take something called business math twice.

sentences.en: But I recently joked to a group of fellow alumni that one of the best parts of Hamilton for me was not knowing how it would end, and nobody didn't know what I was talking about.

sentences.zh: 日，因为这感觉就像全年无休都在滚动发生一样。

sentences.zh: 某种程度上确实如此。

sentences.zh: 是的，一月有大屠杀纪念日，但春天也有大屠杀纪念日（Yom HaShoah）。

sentences.en: And in November, the commemoration of Kristallnacht, which is the event that is acknowledged as
sentences.zh: 而在十一月，则是对水晶之夜的纪念，这一事件被公认为

sentences.en: the official beginning of the Holocaust, the night that the windows of Jewish businesses, homes, and synagogues were smashed by Nazis while the German authorities looked on without
sentences.zh: 大屠杀的正式开始，那一晚，犹太人的企业、住宅和犹太教堂的窗户被纳粹砸碎，而德国当局在一旁袖手旁观，

sentences.en: intervening.
sentences.zh: 没有进行干预。

sentences.en: It was also later than any of us would like to acknowledge that I realized Nazi hunting, a field I believe I had the natural talents to dominate, might be an industry in decline.
sentences.zh: 也是在我们所有人都愿意承认的较晚时候，我才意识到纳粹搜捕这个我曾认为自己拥有统治天赋的领域，可能是一个日渐式微的行业。

sentences.en: I was not a good enough math student to have considered that all the Nazis would be dead by now.

sentences.zh: 正是那一连串精妙的巧合、英雄主义壮举和善意，才让他今天能够在美国的安稳之所向我重新讲述这一切。

sentences.en: The exquisite set of coincidences and acts of heroism and kindness that allowed him to be retelling it to me today from the safety of his perch in America.
sentences.zh: 在林登布拉特先生七岁生日那天，母亲像往常一样带他去面包店吃栗子泥配鲜奶油，这是一道匈牙利美食。

sentences.en: On Mr. Lindenblatt's seventh birthday, his mother took him to the bakery for chestnut puree with whipped cream, a Hungarian delicacy, same as she always did.
sentences.zh: 但今年，当他们吃完时，已经过了针对该镇犹太人新颁布的宵禁时间。

sentences.en: But this year, by the time they were finished, it was past the new curfew that had been levied on the town's Jews.
sentences.zh: 她让他脱下黄星，藏在大衣底下，跟着她走到火车前面，在那里他们可以假装自己不是犹太人。

sentences.en: She told him to take off his yellow star, hide it under his coat, and follow her to the front of the train, where they would pretend they weren't Jews.
sentences.zh: 这让他觉得毫无道理。

sentences.en: It made no sense to him.
sentences.zh: 他深爱着那颗犹太星。

sentences.en: He loved that Jewish star.
sentences.zh: 他为身为

sentences.en: He was so proud to be
sentences.zh: 犹太人感到无比自豪。

sentences.en: Jewish.
sentences.zh: 不过，他还是听了母亲的话。

sentences.en: He listened to his mother, though.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲很聪明。

sentences.en: She was clever, his mother.
sentences.zh: 她总是在想方设法在布达佩斯日益恶化的现实中生存下去。但正如每一部大屠杀故事的走向一样，迅速恶化的局势变得更加糟糕。

sentences.en: She was always figuring out how to live in the worsening reality of BudapeSt. But as it goes in every Holocaust story, worsening quickly got worse.
sentences.zh: 违反宵禁变得越来越难。

sentences.en: It became harder to violate curfew.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生的父亲被带到了一个强迫劳动营。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt's father was taken to a forced labor camp.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生的母亲被迫独自支撑这个家，而七岁的林登布拉特先生现在成了家里的顶梁柱。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt's mother was left to fend for the family, and seven-year-old Mr. Lindenblatt was now the man of the house.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，一条命令下达了。

sentences.en: Then one day, an order came.
sentences.zh: 所有16岁到56岁的女性都必须到火车站报到。

sentences.en: Every woman from the age of 16 to 56 had to report to the train station.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲去拿她的绿色冬大衣，想从口袋里掏出一些钱留给他们。

sentences.en: His mother went to get her green winter coat to take some money from her pocket and leave it for them.
sentences.zh: 但当要穿上大衣出发时，她看了儿子们一眼，意识到自己无法离开他们。

sentences.en: But when it was time to put on the coat and go, she took one look at her sons and realized she couldn't leave them.
sentences.zh: 她收起了大衣，林登布拉特先生向窗外望去。

sentences.en: She put away her coat, and Mr. Lindenblatt looked out the window.
sentences.zh: 他说，他看到妇女们在走路。

sentences.en: He saw women walking, he said.
sentences.zh: 她们正被手持步枪的青少年驱赶到多瑙河边。

sentences.en: They were being led to the Danube by teenagers with rifles.
sentences.zh: 一旦到了河边，她们就会被五个人一组地绑起来。

sentences.en: Once they were at the river, they would be tied up, five per group.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利纳粹会枪杀其中一两个人，然后把整组人推入河中，任由水流将他们冲走，而活着的人则与死尸绑在一起慢慢溺亡。

sentences.en: The Hungarian Nazis would shoot one or two and then push the entire group into the river to let the current take them, as the living drowned, attached to the dead.
sentences.zh: 纳粹开始敲门并搜捕犹太人将他们送往多瑙河畔。

sentences.en: The Nazis began knocking on doors and rounding up Jews to send down the Danube.
sentences.zh: 一天，当他们逼近时，林登布拉特先生的母亲惊慌失措地对他说：“你知道怎么诵经吗，念诵《阿维努·马尔凯努》（Avinu Malkenu）。”

sentences.en: One day, as they approached, Mr. Lindenblatt's mother, frantic, told him, you know how to daven, say the Avinu Malkenu.
sentences.zh: 《阿维努·马尔凯努》是犹太礼拜仪式中最神圣的祈祷文，是一首在犹太重要节日期间向上帝祈求慈悲的祷告。

sentences.en: The Avinu Malkenu is the holiest prayer in Jewish liturgy, a prayer for God's mercy recited on high holidays.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生开始背诵这段祈祷文，那天德国人搜查到离林登布拉特家仅几步之遥的房子时便停了下来。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt began to recite the prayer, and the Germans stopped their rounds that day at the house just short of the Lindenblatts.
sentences.zh: 几个月过去了。

sentences.en: Months went by.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特一家搬到了林登布拉特先生祖母的住所，该地区最终成为了布达佩斯的犹太人隔离区。被称为“箭十字党”的匈牙利纳粹部队

sentences.en: The Lindenblatts moved to Mr. Lindenblatt's grandmother's house in what eventually became the Jewish ghetto in BudapeSt. Troops of Hungarian Nazis, called the Arrow Cross,
sentences.zh: 继续挨家挨户搜查，将犹太人送往集中营或多瑙河畔更直接的死亡之地。

sentences.en: continued to go house to house, sending Jews off to concentration camps or the more immediate death of the Danube.
sentences.zh: 又一次，当他们靠近房门时，林登布拉特先生的母亲恳求儿子背诵《阿维努·马尔凯努》。

sentences.en: Once again, as they approached the door, Mr. Lindenblatt's mother beseeched her son to recite the Avinu Malkenu.
sentences.zh: 他照做了。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他倾尽全心去念，他们又一次停下了，依然是差一点就到门口时停下了。

sentences.en: He said it with all his heart, and they stopped again, again, just short of their door.
sentences.zh: 防空警报拉响了。

sentences.en: Air raid sirens would ring out.
sentences.zh: 有一个地下防空洞允许犹太人进入，但仅限于一个荒谬地由玻璃屋顶覆盖的区域。

sentences.en: There was an underground bomb shelter that allowed Jews, but only in a section that was covered, absurdly, by a glass roof.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上

sentences.en: Each night,
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生都会看着头顶飞过的飞机以及它们投下的炸弹构成的全景画面。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt would watch a panorama of planes flying overhead and the bombs they were dropping.
sentences.zh: 当他谈起这件事时，他仿佛依然能看到那一幕。

sentences.en: He could still see it now, as he talked about it.
sentences.zh: 他又回到了那个时候，仿佛很容易就能看出他小时候长什么样。

sentences.en: He was there again, and it was easy to see what he looked like as a child.
sentences.zh: 当他看着那场灯光秀时，他的双眼闪烁着光芒。

sentences.en: His eyes lit up as he watched the light show.
sentences.zh: 十一月，林登布拉特先生的母亲托人给劳改营里的父亲带信，说家里出事了。

sentences.en: In November, Mr. Lindenblatt's mother got word to his father in the labor camp that the family was in trouble at home.
sentences.zh: 于是他贿赂了一些守卫，在一个夜晚偷偷溜了出来。

sentences.en: And so he bribed some guards and sneaked out one night.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生的父亲赶到公寓，发现妻子正在与负责该栋建筑的匈牙利非犹太人房东争吵，房东正试图把他们赶出去。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt's father arrived at the apartment to find his wife arguing with the Hungarian Gentile in charge of the building, who was trying to evict them.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生的父亲把整个钱袋都拿出来交给那个人。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt's father offered his entire money belt to the man.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生不知道里面有多少钱，只说全拿去吧，为了拯救家人他绝不会要求把钱要回来。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt doesn't know how much money was in there, and said to take it, that he would never ask for it back to help save his family.
sentences.zh: 但那个人把钱袋扔进厨房的炉子里烧掉了，说他的钱毫无用处，而且他不会做任何事来帮助林登布拉特一家。

sentences.en: But the man put the belt into the kitchen stove and burned it, saying his money was useless, and that he would do nothing to help the Lindenblatts.
sentences.zh: 他们无法留下，却又无处可去。

sentences.en: They couldn't stay, but there was also nowhere to go.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生的父亲必须返回劳改营，于是林登布拉特先生、他的母亲和兄弟们只能自己想办法。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatt's father was due back in the camp, so Mr. Lindenblatt and his mother and brothers were left to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 他们踏入了寒冷黑暗的夜晚，注定要前往天知道哪里。

sentences.en: They headed out into the cold, dark night, destined for God knows where.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏板块的字谜游戏《Connections》，我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天都创作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》这两款游戏。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的奇妙特质。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时，我会看到颜色。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的这些人一样的心智创作的。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 加上 games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 我出生于1975年，来到这样一个世界：大屠杀影响过的人在我看来已经非常苍老，而那场战争仿佛是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: I was born in 1975, into a world where the people affected by the Holocaust seemed very old to me, and the war seemed a very long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我出生于1975年，在一个大屠杀受害者对当时的我觉得无比苍老、战争仿佛已过去极久的世界里长大。

sentences.en: But now I'm almost 50, and I realize that I am just about as old as my grandparents were when I was born, and that the period between my birth and the Holocaust
sentences.zh: 但现在我快50岁了，我意识到我的年龄差不多和我祖母出生时一样大，而我出生与大屠杀之间的时间间隔

sentences.en: is roughly the same as between now and the Challenger explosion.
sentences.zh: 大致相当于现在与挑战者号爆炸之间的时间间隔。

sentences.en: I am not an old lady, and the Challenger tragedy still seems awfully recent to me.
sentences.zh: 我可不是什么老太太，可挑战者号悲剧在我看来依然历历在目。

sentences.en: What it must have been like to try to explain all these things to children who simply had lucked out by being born when they were born.
sentences.zh: 向那些刚好在那个时期出生的幸运孩子们解释这一切，当时的情形会是怎样呢？

sentences.en: How I should have understood that I was hearing recent history.
sentences.zh: 我本该明白，我听到的正是近代史。

sentences.en: How I should have understood that a lifetime ago is not actually a very long period of time.
sentences.zh: 我本该明白，一辈子前其实并不是一段很长的时间。

sentences.en: Those who survived left Europe, for the most part.
sentences.zh: 那些幸存者大多离开了欧洲。

sentences.en: They fled to Israel, to South Africa, to Australia, to America.
sentences.zh: 他们逃往以色列、南非、澳大利亚和美国。

sentences.en: They became congressmen and industrial designers.
sentences.zh: 他们成了国会议员和工业设计师。

sentences.en: They composed operas and pioneered electronic music.
sentences.zh: 他们创作歌剧，开创了电子音乐的先河。

sentences.en: They won the Nobel Prizes for Peace and for
sentences.zh: 他们获得了诺贝尔和平奖和

sentences.en: Literature and Economics.
sentences.zh: 文学奖以及经济学奖。

sentences.en: They won the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们荣获了总统自由勋章。

sentences.en: They were best-selling authors and celebrated pianists.
sentences.zh: 他们是畅销书作家和著名的钢琴家。

sentences.en: They helped legalize abortion.
sentences.zh: 他们推动了堕胎合法化。

sentences.en: They won Oscars.
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了奥斯卡奖。

sentences.en: They were therapists and doctors, teachers, and factory workers.
sentences.zh: 他们是治疗师、医生、教师和工厂工人。

sentences.en: My maternal grandparents—let me just remember my own family here for a minute—were named Joseph and Raya Turko.
sentences.zh: 我的外祖父母——请允许我在这里花点时间回忆一下我自己的家人——名字叫约瑟夫（Joseph）和雷娅·图尔科（Raya Turko）。

sentences.en: I was given my Hebrew middle name,
sentences.zh: 我的希伯来语中间名是

sentences.en: Leah, after Joseph's sister, who was killed in the Lodz ghetto.
sentences.zh: 莉亚（Leah），这是为了纪念约瑟夫的妹妹，她在罗兹犹太隔离区遇害。

sentences.en: My mother is named after his mother,
sentences.zh: 我母亲的名字取自他的母亲，

sentences.en: Rachel, who shared her daughter's fate.
sentences.zh: 蕾切尔（Rachel），她和女儿有着同样的命运。

sentences.en: My grandmother, Raya, was on the last train out of
sentences.zh: 我的外祖母雷娅，搭上了从

sentences.en: Kiev before the Babi Yar massacre, the largest killing spree the Nazis carried out, murdering 33,771 people over two days.
sentences.zh: 基辅驶出的最后一班火车，随后便发生了巴比亚尔大屠杀——这是纳粹实施的最大规模屠杀，在两天内谋杀了33,771人。

sentences.en: My grandfather fled Lodz to Bukhara, where he met my grandmother's mother, who hired him to sell ice cream, of all things, on the black market.
sentences.zh: 我的外祖父从罗兹逃到布哈拉，在那里遇到了我外祖母的母亲。当时，老人家竟然雇他在黑市上卖冰淇淋。

sentences.en: When the communists caught him, they sent him to a work camp in Siberia.
sentences.zh: 当共产党人抓到他时，把他送到了西伯利亚的一个劳改营。

sentences.en: He got out, married his employer's daughter, had my mother and my aunt, and emigrated to Israel in 1950 and then to America in 1962.
sentences.zh: 他逃了出来，娶了雇主的女儿，生下了我母亲和阿姨，并于1950年移民以色列，1962年移民美国。

sentences.en: Here, my grandfather was a house painter.
sentences.zh: 来到这里后，我外祖父成了一名油漆工。

sentences.en: My grandmother was an architect, which was what she had studied in Kiev before the war.
sentences.zh: 我外祖母是一名建筑师，这是她在战前于基辅所学的专业。

sentences.en: Their children had children, and they were devoted, excellent grandparents.
sentences.zh: 他们的孩子又有了孩子，他们是非常慈爱、优秀的祖父母。

sentences.en: They bought a dinette store called Sam the Chrome King at the corner
sentences.zh: 他们在

sentences.en: Atlantic Avenue and Eastern Parkway.
sentences.zh: 大西洋大道（Atlantic Avenue）和东公园大道（Eastern Parkway）的转角处，买下了一家名为“铬王山姆”（Sam the Chrome King）的小餐桌椅店。

sentences.en: It's something else now, but the Sam the Chrome King sign was still under the new sign, last I checked.
sentences.zh: 现在那里已经成了别的店铺，但据我上次查看，在新的招牌底下依然能看到“铬王山姆”的招牌。

sentences.en: But that's all I know.
sentences.zh: 然而，我所知道的也就这么多了。

sentences.en: In my family, we never spoke about the war.
sentences.zh: 在我的家族中，我们从未谈论过战争。

sentences.en: The war was an assassin that stood over us, threatening to shoot if we looked it in the eye.
sentences.zh: 战争就像是一个站在我们头顶的刺客，威胁着只要我们敢直视它的眼睛，它就会开枪。

sentences.en: But it was there.
sentences.zh: 但它确实存在。

sentences.en: It was there when my grandmother wouldn't leave any food on the table and combined all the remaining liquids into one glass and drank them.
sentences.zh: 当外祖母不肯在桌上留下任何食物，把所有剩下的汤水倒进一个杯子里喝掉时，它就在那里。

sentences.en: It was there when my grandfather told me he didn't believe in God, because what kind of God would allow a war like that to happen?
sentences.zh: 当外祖父告诉我他不相信上帝，因为什么样的上帝会容许这样的战争发生时，它就在那里。

sentences.en: In those moments, I glimpsed into the window of their suffering and saw a universe of pain with no floor or ceiling.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，我窥见了他们苦难的窗户，看到了一个既无地板也无天花板的痛苦世界。

sentences.en: Some survivors, like Mr. Lindenblatt, made it their mission to make sure the world knew what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 一些幸存者，比如林登布拉特先生（Mr. Lindenblatt），将确保世界了解他们遭遇的不幸视为自己的使命。

sentences.en: My family lived at the opposite end of the spectrum, which is no moral failing of theirs, but it probably is why I spent so long not even knowing to identify myself
sentences.zh: 我的家族则处于光谱的另一端，这并非他们的道德过失，但这可能就是为什么我花了那么长时间，甚至都不知道将自己识别为

sentences.en: as from a survivor family.
sentences.zh: 幸存者家族成员的原因。

sentences.en: This is apparently a common point of view, though it is a bad one, according to people who know better.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是一种很常见的观点，不过在那些见多识广的人看来，这并不是个好观点。

sentences.en: My family being murdered during and as a result of the Holocaust makes the people in my family who made it out survivors.
sentences.zh: 我的家人在大屠杀期间及作为大屠杀的结果而被谋杀，这使得我们家族中那些逃过一劫的人成为了幸存者。

sentences.en: Often, while I was writing this article, I would hear about people who don't identify as survivors because they hid in barns or forests for weeks.
sentences.zh: 在我写这篇文章的过程中，我经常听到有人说他们不觉得自己是幸存者，因为他们只是在谷仓或森林里躲藏了几个星期。

sentences.en: You ate from a pig's trough?
sentences.zh: 你吃过猪食槽里的东西吗？

sentences.en: Someone said to me while I was writing this story.
sentences.zh: 在我写这个故事时，有人曾这样对我说。

sentences.en: You're a survivor.
sentences.zh: 你就是个幸存者。

sentences.en: So what now?
sentences.zh: 那接下来呢？

sentences.en: My grandparents are gone.
sentences.zh: 我的外祖父母已经离世了。

sentences.en: So are all their friends.
sentences.zh: 他们的朋友也全都离去了。

sentences.en: What is the obligation of the people who came after, those who survived the survivors, who carry the story, who carry the residual trauma and haunted memories of their families?
sentences.zh: 后来人的责任是什么呢？那些幸存者的幸存者，那些承载着故事、背负着家族残留创伤和挥之不去记忆的人们？

sentences.en: The people I grew up among were either what's known as 2G, the generation born to Holocaust survivors, or 3G, their grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 与我一同长大的人，要么被称为2G（即大屠杀幸存者生下的第二代），要么被称为3G（他们的孙辈）。

sentences.en: Ilana is 2G on both sides.
sentences.zh: 伊拉娜（Ilana）的父母双方都是2G。

sentences.en: I'm 3G on my mother's side.
sentences.zh: 我母亲这一支是3G。

sentences.en: My father's parents were born in America.
sentences.zh: 我父亲的父母出生在美国。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblatts' mother gave a farmer her wedding ring in exchange for a roll of pig fat.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生的母亲把自己的结婚戒指给了一个农民，换来了一卷猪油。

sentences.en: She cut it into three pieces and gave one to each of her sons, telling them they must eat it.
sentences.zh: 她把它切成三块，每个儿子分一块，并告诉他们必须吃掉。

sentences.en: It was the first time in their lives they'd ever eaten treif.
sentences.zh: 这是他们生平第一次吃非犹太洁食。

sentences.en: The place was freezing and packed.
sentences.zh: 那个地方冰冷刺骨而且拥挤不堪。

sentences.en: One of Mr. Lindenblatts' cousins had a piece of soap in the shelter.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生的一个表亲在避难所里有一块肥皂。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblat thought the soap looked delicious.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特觉得这块肥皂看起来太诱人了。

sentences.en: He would stand on his bed and beg and cry for it.
sentences.zh: 他会站在自己的床上，又求又哭地想要它。

sentences.en: When he finally went to bed, he dreamed of eating the soap, and in those dreams, bubbles came out of his mouth.
sentences.zh: 当他终于上床睡觉时，他梦见自己在吃肥皂，在那些梦里，有泡泡从他嘴里冒出来。

sentences.en: When they ran out of money, they were forced to leave.
sentences.zh: 当他们的钱花光时，他们被迫离开了。

sentences.en: They ended up at a Swiss protective house, an apartment building where Mr. Lindenblatts' grandmother also was staying.
sentences.zh: 他们最终来到了一处瑞士避难所，这是一栋公寓楼，林登布拉特先生的祖母也住在那里。

sentences.en: And then one day, the Russians came through with guns and flashlights.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，苏联人带着枪和手电筒闯了进来。

sentences.en: They'd fought the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 他们与纳粹进行了战斗。

sentences.en: The war was over.
sentences.zh: 战争结束了。

sentences.en: The Lindenblatts were free.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特一家自由了。

sentences.en: The Germans left Hungary, and the Russians took over.
sentences.zh: 德国人撤出了匈牙利，苏联人接管了这里。

sentences.en: Communism wasn't as bad as Nazi occupation, but it wasn't great.
sentences.zh: 共产主义虽然不如纳粹占领那么糟糕，但也算不上多好。

sentences.en: The Lindenblatts rebuilt the cheese wholesale business, now selling a million other things—chicken, milk, eggs, meat, handkerchiefs.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特一家重建了奶酪批发业务，如今他们还销售上百万种其他商品——鸡肉、牛奶、鸡蛋、肉类、手帕。

sentences.en: But people were no longer permitted to have private businesses.
sentences.zh: 但人们不再被允许拥有私人企业。

sentences.en: The communists took their keys and ran them out of their own store.
sentences.zh: 共产党人拿走了他们的钥匙，把他们赶出了自己的店铺。

sentences.en: Little Mr. Lindenblatts was regularly beaten up at school for being Jewish and got into trouble for not attending on Saturdays.
sentences.zh: 小林登布拉特经常在学校因为是犹太人而遭到殴打，并因周六不去上学而惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: The Hungarian Revolution came in 1956.
sentences.zh: 1956年，匈牙利革命爆发了。

sentences.en: Soon after that, he escaped, first to Austria, then to Israel, and then to America, where his parents and brothers were waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，他逃离了出去，先是到了奥地利，然后是以色列，最后到了美国，他的父母和兄弟们正在那里等着他。

sentences.en: He came and worked in his brother Robert's camera shop, met Miriam, who worked for Robert as a girl Friday and would become our Mr. Lindenblatts' wife.
sentences.zh: 他来到他哥哥罗伯特的照相馆工作，遇到了米丽娅姆。米丽娅姆年轻时曾为罗伯特做过杂务女工，后来成为了我们所熟知的林登布拉特先生的妻子。

sentences.en: She was also Hungarian.
sentences.zh: 她也是匈牙利人。

sentences.en: Her mother was at Auschwitz and her father in a forced labor camp.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲曾在奥斯威辛，父亲则在强迫劳动营。

sentences.en: Mrs. Lindenblatts' father had nine siblings and her mother had four.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特太太有九个兄弟姐妹，她母亲有四个。

sentences.en: Both lost their parents and all but one of their siblings.
sentences.zh: 两人都失去了父母以及除了一个之外的所有兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: Mrs. Lindenblatts was so happy to marry another
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特太太非常高兴能嫁给另一个

sentences.en: Hungarian.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利人。

sentences.en: Who else would understand what her family had been through?
sentences.zh: 除了他，还有谁能理解她的家族所经历的一切呢？

sentences.en: Who would share the burden of the anxiety of knowing what kind of evil is out there?
sentences.zh: 谁能分担那种焦虑的负担：深知外界存在着何等可怕的邪恶？

sentences.en: Who would agree that the children should have passports just about as soon as they were taken out of the nursery at the hospital?
sentences.zh: 谁会赞同孩子们刚被从医院的婴儿室抱出来，就应该立刻办好护照？

sentences.en: The Lindenblatts sent their daughters to Jewish schools.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特夫妇将女儿们送去了犹太学校。

sentences.en: They went to synagogue each week, kept a kosher home.
sentences.zh: 他们每周去犹太会堂，保持着犹太洁食的家庭饮食习惯。

sentences.en: This was where Alana one day came home with the poem she wrote about death via a Nazi firing squad.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，阿兰娜有一天带回来一首诗，写的是死于纳粹行刑队之手。

sentences.en: All these years later, when I visited her, I saw it again.
sentences.zh: 多年后，当我拜访她时，我又看到了它。

sentences.en: I said to her, see, this is the exact thing I object to.
sentences.zh: 我对她说，你看，这就是我反对的地方。

sentences.en: Look at you, ten years old, being asked to imagine a girl's death by a firing squad.
sentences.zh: 看看你，十岁的时候，却被要求去想象一个女孩死于行刑队枪决的场景。

sentences.en: Look at how they framed it.
sentences.zh: 看看他们是怎么包装这事的。

sentences.en: And she said, no, they framed it because they were proud of me.
sentences.zh: 而她说，不，他们这样包装是因为他们为我感到骄傲。

sentences.en: And I said, exactly, they were proud of your death poem.
sentences.zh: 我说，没错，他们为你的死亡诗歌感到骄傲。

sentences.en: But she shook her head and laughed a little and said she didn't really understand what I was talking about.
sentences.zh: 但她摇了摇头，笑了笑，说她其实并不明白我在说什么。

sentences.en: And now that I'm writing it, now that I've been doing this for a few months, honestly, neither do I.
sentences.zh: 而现在，当我把这些写下来，当我做这件事已经好几个月之后，说实话，我也不明白了。

sentences.en: Survivor Stories was set to debut to the public on January 27th, which is the anniversary of the liberation of Auschwitz.
sentences.zh: 《幸存者故事》原定于1月27日向公众首映，这一天是奥斯威辛集中营解放纪念日。

sentences.en: The Museum of Jewish Heritage holds an annual gathering of survivors on that day.
sentences.zh: 犹太遗产博物馆在那一天会举办一年一度的幸存者聚会。

sentences.en: And this year, the 80th anniversary, would host a simulcast of the live ceremony from Poland, followed by a demonstration of the technology.
sentences.zh: 而今年作为80周年纪念，将同步转播来自波兰的现场仪式，随后还将进行技术演示。

sentences.en: There were 200 or so survivors gathered, as well as some of their children and spouses and home health aides.
sentences.zh: 现场聚集了大约200名幸存者，还有一些他们的子女、配偶以及家庭保健护工。

sentences.en: It was a good crowd.
sentences.zh: 这是一场规模不错的聚会。

sentences.en: But in a few years, there won't be enough people left to fill the room, which is not even the largest room in the museum.
sentences.zh: 但在几年后，将不再剩下足够的人来填满这个房间，而这甚至还不是博物馆里最大的房间。

sentences.en: Branya Brandman was there.
sentences.zh: 布兰娅·布兰德曼也在场。

sentences.en: We talked about her time recording her interview, and as she was describing it to me, I learned that she had been sent to the gas chamber seven separate times.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了她录制采访时的经历，而在她向我描述的过程中，我得知她曾七次被送进毒气室。

sentences.en: And at the last minute, each time had evaded it.
sentences.zh: 并且每一次都在最后一分钟逃脱了。

sentences.en: I had missed this in my interrogation of the survivor stories.
sentences.zh: 我在审视幸存者故事时漏掉了这一点。

sentences.en: It's another one of those questions you wouldn't think to ask.
sentences.zh: 这是那种你根本不会想到去问的问题。

sentences.en: The simulcast began.
sentences.zh: 转播开始了。

sentences.en: In Poland, the ceremony was taking place at the actual gates of the concentration camp.
sentences.zh: 在波兰，仪式正集中营的真正大门前举行。

sentences.en: It was attended by fewer than 50 survivors and a handful of world leaders.
sentences.zh: 出席的幸存者不到50人，还有少数几位世界领导人。

sentences.en: Ours was not in attendance.
sentences.zh: 我们这儿没有出席。

sentences.en: The audience in Manhattan sat in rapt attention.
sentences.zh: 曼哈顿的观众全神贯注地坐着。

sentences.en: A man named Boris Vineker held a framed painting he made of a Nazi crematory.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫鲍里斯·维内克的男子拿着一幅他画的纳粹焚尸炉的装裱画。

sentences.en: The smoke coming out of it filled with music notes and science and math equations, all the
sentences.zh: 里面冒出的烟雾中充满了音符、科学和数学公式——所有那些大屠杀烈士们如果不是被

sentences.en: potential contributions to society that the martyrs of the Holocaust might have made, had they not been loSt. On the back was a poem he'd written called Never Again.
sentences.zh: 杀害，本可能为社会做出的潜在贡献。背面写着他创作的一首名为《绝不再发生》的诗。

sentences.en: A terrible crime and a worldwide shame.
sentences.zh: 一场可怕的罪行和世界的耻辱。

sentences.en: The Jews have been burned in oven flame, it went.
sentences.zh: 犹太人在炉火中被焚烧，诗中写道。

sentences.en: Why this happened?
sentences.zh: 为什么会发生这一切？

sentences.en: Whom to blame?
sentences.zh: 该怪谁？

sentences.en: Let's repeat, never again.
sentences.zh: 让我们重申，绝不再发生。

sentences.en: Never again.
sentences.zh: 绝不再发生。

sentences.en: During a pause between speakers, I asked a man sitting near me what had brought him here.
sentences.zh: 在演讲者之间的间隙，我问坐在附近的一个人是什么把他带到这里来的。

sentences.en: But instead of telling me that story, he told me his whole story, which was perhaps the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但没有告诉我那个故事，他向我讲述了他整个人生故事，这或许也是一回事。

sentences.en: His name is Eugene Ginter, and as a child he had gone on what he called a tour of the different hotels, spending time in the Plasho ghetto and then the Plasho concentration camp,
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫尤金·金特尔，他还是个孩子时，曾经历过他所说的“不同酒店之旅”，先是在普拉绍夫犹太隔离区度过了一段时间，然后是普拉绍夫集中营，

sentences.en: then Gross Rosen, then Brunlitz, then Auschwitz-Birkenau, and then was liberated in Auschwitz I, the original camp.
sentences.zh: 接着是格罗斯-罗森，然后是布伦利茨，再到奥斯威辛-比克瑙，最后在最初的集中营奥斯威辛一号获释。

sentences.en: He had been separated from his mother but was able to stay with his father for much of his imprisonment.
sentences.zh: 他曾与母亲失散，但在大部分关押期间得以和父亲待在一起。

sentences.en: At Gross Rosen, he was stripped naked and made to sit with his naked father on the ground, among hundreds of others.
sentences.zh: 在格罗斯-罗森，他被剥光衣服，被迫和赤身裸体的父亲一起坐在地上，周围还有成百上千的人。

sentences.en: Guards shaved their hair into a reverse mohawk, just to humiliate them, he said, just to dehumanize them.
sentences.zh: 守卫把他们的头发剃成逆莫霍克发型，他说，纯粹是为了羞辱他们，纯粹是为了剥夺他们的人性。

sentences.en: He was subjected to a cavity search.
sentences.zh: 他经受了体腔搜查。

sentences.en: They were given a hot shower, then made to run through the snow to see who would get pneumonia and be sent to the gas chamber immediately.
sentences.zh: 他们洗了个热水澡，然后被迫在雪地里奔跑，看看谁会得肺炎并被立即送往毒气室。

sentences.en: He told me how it took two weeks to get to Auschwitz-Birkenau from Krakow in the cattle car he was put into, though it's only a one-hour drive as the crow flies.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他所坐的运牛车从克拉科夫到奥斯威辛-比克瑙花了两个星期，尽管按直线距离计算开车只需要一个小时。

sentences.en: On the way, his father took a diamond he'd secreted and traded it to a guard for two bottles of vodka and told Eugene
sentences.zh: 在路上，他的父亲拿出了一颗藏匿的钻石，跟一个守卫换了两瓶伏特加，并告诉尤金

sentences.en: to drink it because it would kill the typhus that was going around the camp, which, if he caught it, would also get him sent to the gas chamber.
sentences.zh: 把它喝下去，因为这能杀死营地里肆虐的斑疹伤寒，如果染上这种病，他也会被送进毒气室。

sentences.en: He was five years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时五岁。

sentences.en: He was taken on a long, slow march to the main Auschwitz camp, and whoever was in the back of the line would be shot, so he kept running up to be at the front of the line.
sentences.zh: 他被带去参加了一场漫长而缓慢的行军，前往奥斯威辛主集中营，队伍后面的人会被枪杀，所以他一直往前跑，想待在队伍最前面。

sentences.en: When finally he was liberated, he was taken to a hospital back in Krakow.
sentences.zh: 当他最终获释时，他被送回克拉科夫的一家医院。

sentences.en: Later, he was sent to an orphanage, where parents would come looking for their displaced children.
sentences.zh: 后来，他被送到了一家孤儿院，父母们会来那里寻找他们失散的孩子。

sentences.en: He was sitting on the top floor, his legs dangling out the window with some of the
sentences.zh: 他正坐在顶楼，双腿悬挂在窗外，跟其他一些

sentences.en: other boys, when someone came in to tell him his mother was downstairs, but we had to stop talking
sentences.zh: 男孩在一起，这时有人进来告诉他他的母亲在楼下，但我们不得不停止交谈

sentences.en: because there were some speakers at the event, and the president of the museum was going to make a speech.
sentences.zh: 因为活动中有了一些发言嘉宾，博物馆馆长将要发表讲话。

sentences.en: And that was fine by me because I had sunk into what was a now-familiar speechlessness,
sentences.zh: 这倒也合我心意，因为我已经陷入了一种现在变得有些熟悉的失语状态中，

sentences.en: one that never changes in the face of the distressing glimpse of what humanity is capable of, of what a person is asked to live with, of how it changes them forever.
sentences.zh: 面对人类所能作恶的惨烈一幕，面对一个人被要求承受的一切，面对这一切如何永远改变了他们，这种失语状态从未改变。

sentences.en: It is this speechlessness, or maybe just the blessed limits of my imagination, or the blessed limits of my abilities as an interviewer.
sentences.zh: 正是这种失语状态，或者说仅仅是我想象力的有福极限，亦或是作为一名采访者的能力极限。

sentences.en: That stops me from knowing how to ask questions that will yield stories like this.
sentences.zh: 这让我不知道该如何提出能引出这类故事的问题。

sentences.en: That is the problem with the HolocauSt. Though, of course, not its main problem,
sentences.zh: 这就是大屠杀的问题所在。当然，这并不是它最主要的问题，

sentences.en: which was that it was the HolocauSt. The problem is that you could grow up thinking about it all the time and still not even be able to imagine how bad it was.
sentences.zh: 最主要的问题是它毕竟是大屠杀。问题在于，你可以从小到大一直在思考它，却依然无法想象它究竟有多糟。

sentences.en: There is no bottom to the depths of cruelty and depravity that you can learn about if you just ask the right question of the kind, calm man sitting next to you.
sentences.zh: 只要你向坐在你身旁那位温和、平静的男士提出正确的问题，你就会了解到深不见底的残酷与堕落。

sentences.en: But you have had such a privileged life that you don't even know which questions to ask.
sentences.zh: 但你过着如此优渥的生活，甚至不知道该问哪些问题。

sentences.en: And the questions I can formulate are so rude and raw that they threaten to make life just a little more awful than it is right now for someone who has, frankly, been put
sentences.zh: 而我能构思出的问题又是如此粗鲁和生硬，它们可能会让某人的生活变得比现在更加糟糕——说实话，这个人已经经历得够多的了，

sentences.en: through quite enough and does not have to sit for my demoralizing and morbid and even lurid curiosity.
sentences.zh: 根本没必要坐在这里满足我那令人沮丧、病态甚至耸人听闻的好奇心。

sentences.en: Besides, how could any survivor give me a satisfying answer to,
sentences.zh: 此外，任何幸存者又怎么可能给我一个令人满意的答案：

sentences.en: how do you live knowing that people are capable of this?
sentences.zh: 当你知道人们能够做出这种事时，你是怎么活下来的？

sentences.en: Or, do you ever wonder what it means about you or God or fate or coincidence that you were sent there seven times and spared each time?
sentences.zh: 或者，你是否曾想过，自己七次被送去那里却每次都幸免于难，这对于你、对于上帝、命运或巧合意味着什么？

sentences.en: Or,
sentences.zh: 或者，

sentences.en: how can you bear to know the measure of all that this world contains?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能忍受去衡量这一切世界所包含的苦难？

sentences.en: How do you live in a world where you were in a concentration camp while your cousin was on the Wonder Wheel?
sentences.zh: 当你的表亲在坐摩天轮时，你却身处集中营，你如何在这样的世界里生活？

sentences.en: But also, what was the point of all of this Holocaust education if, while you are still alive,
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，如果趁着你们还活着的时候，

sentences.zh: 根据克莱姆斯会议（Claims Conference）的一项调查发现，15%的30岁以下美国成年人认为大屠杀中被谋杀的犹太人数量被严重夸大了，

sentences.en: Jews murdered in the Holocaust is greatly exaggerated, and that 24% believe that fewer than
sentences.zh: 24%的人认为战争期间被杀害的犹太人少于200万，

sentences.en: 2 million Jews were killed during the war and 48% of all American adults surveyed could not name one of
sentences.zh: 48%的受访美国成年人甚至说不出纳粹用来折磨和谋杀犹太人的任何一个集中营、犹太隔离区或其他4.4万多个杀戮地点中的一个，

sentences.en: the concentration camps or ghettos or other of the more than 44,000 killing sites that the Nazis used to torture and murder Jews.
sentences.zh: 那么所有这些大屠杀教育到底有什么意义？

sentences.en: Is there any rational way to explain why, from 2018 to 2023, right here in New
sentences.zh: 有什么理性的方式可以解释为什么从2018年到2023年，就在拥有以色列境外最多犹太人居住的纽约州，

sentences.en: York State, where the largest number of Jews outside of Israel live?
sentences.zh: 针对犹太人的仇恨犯罪激增了89%，以至于在2023年这类犯罪占到了所有仇恨犯罪的44%？

sentences.en: Hate crimes against Jews rose by 89% so that in 2023 they made up 44% of all hate crimes.
sentences.zh: 你看到他们在上西区的罗马犹太会堂（Romamu Synagogue）喷涂的卐字标志了吗？

sentences.en: And did you see the swastika they spray-painted on the
sentences.zh: 或者河滨公园（Riverside Park）某面墙上写着的“去死吧犹太人”？

sentences.en: Romamu Synagogue on the Upper West Side?
sentences.zh: 你听说有人把一块砖头砸进东区一家犹太洁食披萨店的玻璃门吗？

sentences.zh: 一个路人用匈牙利语对同伴说，看那个脏犹太人。

sentences.en: And Mr.
sentences.zh: 而身材高大、体魄健壮的林登布拉特先生

sentences.en: Lindenblatt, tall and athletic, turned to him and he said, what did you just say?
sentences.zh: 转过身对他说，你刚才说什么？

sentences.en: And the man cowered and said, I wasn't talking about you.
sentences.zh: 那个人畏缩着说，我不是在说你。

sentences.en: He volunteered for the Jewish ambulance service because it felt good to help his people when he'd grown up feeling so helpless about what was happening to the Jews around him.
sentences.zh: 他自愿加入犹太救护队，因为每当他看着身边犹太人的遭遇而感到无能为力时，能为自己的人民做点事让他觉得很宽慰。

sentences.en: Alana told me that on 9-11, he ran to St. Vincent's to volunteer as an EMT.
sentences.zh: 阿拉娜告诉我，在“9·11”事件发生时，他跑向圣文森特医院自愿担任急救医疗技术员。

sentences.en: He attended synagogue every week.
sentences.zh: 他每周都去犹太会堂。

sentences.en: He wore a yarmulke all the time because of what an act of defiance it still was to him.
sentences.zh: 他一直戴着犹太圆小帽，因为对他来说，这依然是一种充满挑衅意味的举动。

sentences.en: Religion, if you think about it, he said, is mostly Meshuggah's.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果你仔细想想，宗教大多都是些疯话。

sentences.en: He did it to remind himself and the world that he was allowed to, because it's a fist in the face to the people who tried to kill him and eradicate his people.
sentences.zh: 他这样做是为了提醒自己和全世界，他是被允许这样做的，因为这是给那些企图杀死他、根除他同胞的人的一记当头棒喝。

sentences.en: His family was his revenge against Hitler, as was his marriage, as were his daughters, as were his grandchildren, as was his home, the same one he lived in and was never asked to
sentences.zh: 他的家庭是对希特勒的复仇，他的婚姻也是，他的女儿们也是，他的孙辈们也是，他的家也是——正是他一直居住、从未被要求

sentences.en: leave.
sentences.zh: 离开的那个家。

sentences.en: I survived the Holocaust, he told me.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，我熬过了大屠杀。

sentences.en: I survived the Hungarian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我熬过了匈牙利革命。

sentences.en: I survived 9-11 and a lot of things between.
sentences.zh: 我熬过了“9·11”以及期间的许多事情。

sentences.en: And this is my last stand, though, last to try to survive.
sentences.zh: 这是我最后的阵地，虽然也是最后一次努力求生。

sentences.en: So I'm not giving up.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会放弃。

sentences.en: But then, in January, Alana called me to tell me her father's decline had become more rapid,
sentences.zh: 但随后，在一月，阿拉娜打电话告诉我，她父亲的病情恶化得更快了，

sentences.en: and I went to visit him one last time, to read him this article, in case he didn't live to see it published.
sentences.zh: 于是我去看了他最后一次，读了这篇文章给他听，以防他没能等到文章发表的那一天。

sentences.en: The house was filled when I got there.
sentences.zh: 我到那里时，屋里挤满了人。

sentences.en: The men from the ambulance service came in and out, visiting all day and night, making sure the Lindenblatts had every hospital bed and chair assist they needed.
sentences.zh: 救护队的男人们进进出出，日夜探望，确保林登布拉特夫妇拥有他们所需要的每一张医院病床和椅子辅助设备。

sentences.en: He was now confined to a bed, and he could barely open his eyes to greet me.
sentences.zh: 他当时已经卧床不起，几乎无法睁开眼睛来迎接我。

sentences.en: But he did, with that smile.
sentences.zh: 但他还是睁开了，带着那种标志性的微笑。

sentences.en: The men from the ambulance told me stories about him.
sentences.zh: 救护队的男人们向我讲述了关于他的故事。

sentences.en: There are hundreds of volunteers in the Flatbush region, but for a long time they told me there was only Mr. Lindenblat in Manhattan
sentences.zh: 在夫拉特布什地区有几百名志愿者，但他们告诉我，长久以来在曼哈顿

sentences.en: Beach.
sentences.zh: 海滩只有林登布拉特先生一人。

sentences.en: He took every call there.
sentences.zh: 那里的每一个求助电话都是他接的。

sentences.en: Everyone knew him.
sentences.zh: 所有人都认识他。

sentences.en: Some people, when they were in distress, called his house directly.
sentences.zh: 有些人遇到紧急情况时，会直接打电话到他家里。

sentences.en: They only wanted to be treated by him.
sentences.zh: 他们只愿意接受他的治疗。

sentences.en: The Russians in the area loved him.
sentences.zh: 那里的俄罗斯人非常喜爱他。

sentences.en: He was strong like an ox, one of his fellow volunteers told me, and his patient care was special.
sentences.zh: 他的一位志愿者同伴告诉我，他壮得像头牛，他对病人的照料非常特殊。

sentences.en: The men asked Mr.
sentences.zh: 男人们请求林登布拉特先生

sentences.en: Lindenblat for a blessing, but he wouldn't give it.
sentences.zh: 给予祝福，但他不肯给。

sentences.en: Who is he to give a blessing, he asked.
sentences.zh: 他问，他算什么身份去给予祝福？

sentences.en: He's just a man who has striven, who had faith, who had trusted.
sentences.zh: 他只是一个一直在奋斗、拥有信仰、懂得信任的人。

sentences.en: That's what was asked of him.
sentences.zh: 这就是对他的要求。

sentences.en: It's what he believed is asked of us all.
sentences.zh: 这也是他坚信对我们所有人的要求。

sentences.en: Everyone cleared out, and I read Mr. Lindenblat this article.
sentences.zh: 所有人都离开了，我把这篇文章读给林登布拉特先生听。

sentences.en: For a while, we weren't sure if he could still hear me.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我们不确定他是否还能听到我说话。

sentences.en: His eyes were closed, but he was smiling the whole time.
sentences.zh: 他的眼睛闭着，但在整个过程中他一直微笑着。

sentences.en: When I finished, I told him I was sorry I was late in telling it.
sentences.zh: 我读完后，告诉他我很抱歉把这个故事讲得太晚了。

sentences.en: He shook his head and said the word perfect.
sentences.zh: 他摇了摇头，说出了“完美”这个词。

sentences.en: Less than a week later, he died.
sentences.zh: 不到一周后，他去世了。

sentences.en: Mr. Lindenblat was buried the next day.
sentences.zh: 林登布拉特先生于第二天入土为安。

sentences.en: It seemed as if all of Brooklyn and most of Queens and anyone who came over from Hungary was in the
sentences.zh: 殡仪馆里似乎挤满了整个布鲁克林、大部分皇后区以及所有从匈牙利赶来的人，

sentences.en: funeral home, sharing memories of how he lived to help his community, how he loved his family,
sentences.zh: 大家分享着关于他的记忆：他是如何一生致力于帮助社区，他是如何深爱家人，

sentences.en: how, in the end, he didn't know how to do anything but survive, which was why death was so hard for him to accept.
sentences.zh: 以及到头来，他除了求生什么都不会，这也是为什么死亡对他而言如此难以接受。

sentences.en: When it was time to go to the cemetery, the legion of volunteer EMTs carried his coffin to
sentences.zh: 当到了要去墓地的时候，志愿紧急医疗队方阵将他的灵柩抬到了

sentences.en: one of the ambulances, and, with sirens blaring, led the motorcade to New Jersey, where his body was
sentences.zh: 其中一辆救护车上，伴随着刺耳的警笛声，车队驶向新泽西州，在那里他的遗体

sentences.en: finally laid to reSt. His coffin, a pine box, was placed in the ground, and, as is the tradition, we took turns shoveling dirt onto it until the hole was filled.
sentences.zh: 最终入土为安。他的棺木是一个松木盒，被放入地下，按照传统，我们轮流往上面铲土，直到填满坑洞。

sentences.en: But that last day I saw him, before I left his house, he asked me one last time if I needed to know anything else.
sentences.zh: 但在我离开他家的那天见他的最后一面时，他最后一次问我是否还有需要了解的事情。

sentences.en: I didn't.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: I told him I had no more questions.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他我没有其他问题了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: All I had left was my awe at what he survived.
sentences.zh: 我剩下的只有对他在那些经历中存活下来的惊叹。

sentences.en: What a privilege it was to hear his story, and how lucky I was to know him.
sentences.zh: 能听到他的故事是何等的荣幸，而认识他是多么的幸运。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作，

sentences.en: until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时又扣人心弦的权力争斗中。
